summary: An owner gate no longer shows an execution plan that execution approval would refuse. The new read-only `delivery_compile.py check-plan --delivery DLV-###` runs the checks `approve-execution` runs, through one shared helper, and writes nothing: cycles, duplicate stories, unordered path or contract overlaps, unknown roles, stale pins, the lane and seam rules and the pull request check precondition. The execution-planning flow and entry run it before the standard plan gate, and gate A at `owner_gates` `two_fixed_gates` runs it on the proposal, where an open Operation revision that its approval would take, checked as that approval renders it, is listed under `pending_operation_revisions` with the `source_hash` the approval stamps instead of refused, since gate A approves it first, and one its approval would refuse, such as a draft without `test_command`, is refused with what the approval finds. Any other plan gate approves no open revision, so it refuses one with its revision number and draft status. `operation_compile.py approve` renders the approved text through the same helper. `light-path-check` reports the same findings. Approval semantics do not change.
